nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do the direct effects of individual drivers of biodiversity loss compare to their indirect effects?
nodes.answer: The direct effects of individual drivers have been intensively studied, while the knowledge on indirect effects and interactions among drivers is still limited.

nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What are some of the environmental impacts associated with the production and consumption of UFDs?
nodes.answer: Production and consumption of UFDs determine 26% of total greenhouse gas emissions, 70% of freshwater withdrawals, and 78% of marine and freshwater eutrophication, leading to soil and surface water acidification, loss of biodiversity, and air pollution.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the environmental impact differences between the highest and lowest quartiles of UPF consumption?
nodes.answer: Compared to low UPF consumption, higher UPF consumption was statistically significantly inversely associated with blue water (_x0002_13.6%), GHG emissions (_x0002_7.7%), acid?cation (_x0002_7.2%), marine water eutrophication (_x0002_5.4%), freshwater eutrophication (_x0002_5.3%), and land use (_x0002_3.0%).
